title: malus sylvestris subsp. pumila
intro: Malus sylvestris subsp. pumila, commonly known as the Dwarf Mountain Apple, is a subspecies of wild apple tree native to the mountainous regions of Europe. The Dwarf Mountain Apple is known for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to protect against cell damage and reduce inflammation in the body. Its therapeutic actions include exhibiting antimicrobial and antiproliferative effects, suggesting potential applications in wound healing and cancer prevention. The bioactive constituents of Malus sylvestris subsp. pumila include phenolic acids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
